title:
STATISTICS,
(HISTOGRAMS)
objective: LO: I can draw and interpret histograms with equal and unequal class widths.

content.text: A histogram displays continuous data using bars with no gaps. The frequency density is plotted on the y-axis when class widths are unequal.
Key formula: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. The area of each bar represents the frequency.

examples.expr: Plot frequency on y-axis for unequal widths

examples.desc: gaps are for bar charts, not histograms

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Frequency density = frequency divided by class width. Area of bar = frequency.
key_idea.caption: Area of each bar gives the frequency for that class

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – calculating frequency density
modelled_examples.question: Class 10-20 has frequency 30. Find the frequency density.
modelled_examples.explanation: Divide the frequency by the class width.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – finding frequency from a histogram
modelled_examples.question: A bar has height (density) 4 and width 5. Find the frequency.
modelled_examples.explanation: The area of the bar gives the frequency.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – unequal class widths
modelled_examples.question: Classes 0-10 (freq 15), 10-30 (freq 40). Find densities.
modelled_examples.explanation: Each class has its own width; calculate density separately.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – estimating from a histogram
modelled_examples.question: Estimate how many values fall between 15 and 25 if the density is 3 across that range.
modelled_examples.explanation: Use area to estimate frequencies within part of a class.

practice.heading: Calculating frequency density
practice.instruction: Find the frequency density for each class.

items.statement: The height of a histogram bar always shows the frequency
Histogram bars have no gaps because data is continuous
Wider bars always represent more data
The area of each bar represents the frequency

problems.text: A histogram shows times (minutes): 0-5 (density 4), 5-15 (density 3), 15-30 (density 2), 30-60 (density 1). Find the total number of people surveyed. Estimate how many took between 10 and 20 minutes.
80 students took a test. The results: 0-40 marks (density 0.5), 40-60 marks (density 2), 60-80 marks (density d), 80-100 marks (density 0.75). Find the value of d and estimate the median mark.
